patch.name: forest
patch.title: FOREST, the hidden fifth course
patch.description:
The practice's course selection gets a fifth panel, FOREST: a complete course of the game's ROMs that no menu leads to. Its practice clock runs as the other courses' (60 s, then a credit at each checkpoint), its rival follows its own road, and its race's end plays (the game hung after CLEARED). Its options give it its own panel, title and weather, and another music than MOUNTAIN's to try.
A patch of the program EPROMs (EPR-20632 to EPR-20635), made by Scripts/RomPatches/srally2_forest.py. Whatever options are on, the EPROMs keep their CRCs: the test menu's MEMORY TEST says GOOD.

option.name: title
option.title: FOREST's title before its races
option.description: The title shown while FOREST loads is FOREST's (the patch's own: its photo, its name), not MOUNTAIN's.

option.name: panel
option.title: FOREST's panel
option.description: FOREST's panel in the course selection shows FOREST: a photo of the course and its title, the patch's own, drawn over MOUNTAIN's panel (which FOREST's otherwise is).

option.name: rain
option.title: Rain
option.description: FOREST's weather, SNOWY's falling particles (FOREST's textures have no snowflake: a banner's corner falls instead), falls as rain: a drop of the patch's, faster, spread over its height, none under the rocks of the gorge.

option.name: reflections
option.title: Faint reflections
option.description: The cars' reflections on FOREST take a faint texture of the patch's instead of FOREST's own, far more opaque than the other courses' (white streaks over the car).

option.name: championship
option.title: The championship's fifth stage
option.description: The championship runs DESERT, MOUNTAIN, SNOWY, RIVIERA, then FOREST (its times the game's own); the final results and the name entry show five stages, the fifth labelled FOREST.

option.name: music
option.title: FOREST's music
option.description: The music of FOREST's races: MOUNTAIN's, as the game has it, or another of its tracks. Those no course uses may hold music meant for FOREST (or nothing): listen.
